briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development of the past 24 hours is Israel's significant airstrikes on Hezbollah command centers and infrastructure in Beirut's Dahiyeh district, which resulted in at least two fatalities and eleven injuries. This aggressive action, taken in response to Hezbollah rocket fire into northern Israel, has been met with explicit threats of "decisive and painful" retaliation from senior Iranian officials and Hezbollah, significantly heightening regional escalation risks. Concurrently, US forces intercepted two Iranian drones in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to the growing direct confrontation between the US and Iran.

IRAN
No direct military strikes against Iranian territory have been reported within the last 24 hours. However, US Central Command (CENTCOM) shot down two Iranian one-way attack drones that were threatening maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Foreign Ministry accused the US of "violating ceasefire" and "military aggression" for a US drone strike on radar facilities in Sirik and Qeshm on June 6, and the IRGC previously announced retaliatory strikes on US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain on the same date. Fars news agency reported an explosion on Kharg Island, which the IRGC Navy attributed to the neutralization of old munitions.

Internally, Iranian officials have issued strong threats following the Dahiyeh strikes, with the Spokesman for the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission, Ebrahim Rezaee, stating, "Look at the sky over the occupied territories tonight," and the Khatam al-Anbiya Headquarters warning of potential "True Promise 5" operations, possibly targeting Haifa and Tel Aviv. President Trump claimed Iran’s new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, was "severely hurt" but is "more rational" than his father, although an Iranian source stated he was injured in the leg during a previous attack but is now healthy. Student protests against university entrance exam (Konkur) rules occurred in several cities, including Tehran, Mashhad, Isfahan, and Shiraz.

Economically, OPEC+ (including Iran) is meeting to adjust oil output. Iran has begun charging an average of $1.5-2 million per vessel for transit through the Strait of Hormuz, with payments accepted in cash, goods, services, or cryptocurrency (Tether). President Trump claimed Iran loses $400-500 million daily due to the US naval blockade. The US Department of Treasury is reportedly considering using blocked Iranian assets to compensate Gulf states for damages caused by Iranian attacks.

Diplomatically, the US has drafted a resolution for the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Board of Governors, demanding "accurate information" from Iran on bombed nuclear sites and enriched uranium stockpiles. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman, Baghaei, accused the US of "changing and contradictory" positions, stalling negotiations despite ongoing messages exchanged via Pakistani mediators. President Trump stated he would not unfreeze Iranian assets or lift sanctions before a comprehensive agreement but expressed openness to direct talks with Mojtaba Khamenei. Pakistan’s Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi delivered a "special message" from Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to Mojtaba Khamenei, meeting with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted significant airstrikes in Beirut's Dahiyeh district, targeting Hezbollah command centers and infrastructure in response to rocket fire on northern Israel. Strikes were also reported in Tyre, Mijdoun, Jabal al-Rayan, Al-Zararia, and Maarakeh in southern Lebanon, with approximately 150 Hezbollah infrastructure sites reportedly hit over the weekend. The IDF also discovered a substantial underground Hezbollah bunker in Beaufort.

In central Israel, a shooting attack in the Kochav Ya'ir area killed reservist soldier Haim Kalomiti, 55, and severely wounded the Tzur Natan security coordinator, with other individuals sustaining injuries. The attacker was identified as Omer Yassin, 21, from Tayibe, who was subsequently killed by security forces. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir visited the scene and Gaza, where he reaffirmed the military's commitment to "erode Hamas's power" and "disarm Hamas," claiming operational control over 60-70% of the Gaza Strip. The IDF eliminated Sakr Abu Karim, a Nukhba Force commander and leader of the October 7 Kissufim raid, and Muhanad Othman Yassin Farwana, a Hamas cell commander, in southern Gaza.

The Israeli home front experienced rocket interceptions over Yiftah and Ramot Naftali, and hostile aircraft intrusion alerts in Metulla, Misgav Am, and Margaliot, with one drone reportedly falling in southern Lebanon with no injuries. Terrorist infiltration alerts were activated in Tzur Yitzhak and Tzur Natan.

Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz ordered the Dahiyeh strikes, with Netanyahu stating Israel "will not allow Hezbollah to fire on our territory or our settlements, and we will act accordingly." The government approved a plan to house foreign agriculture workers. Debates continue over the "Torah Study Basic Law" and conscription exemptions. The High Court of Justice instructed Justice Minister Levin to cooperate with Supreme Court President Amit. Mossad head Roman Gofman dismissed his deputy, 'A', citing a desire to reshape the senior leadership team. US intelligence reports indicate a heightened counterintelligence threat level from Israeli espionage targeting US officials involved in Iran peace talks.

Civilian impacts include the casualties from the Kochav Ya'ir attack, with schools closed in Tzur Yitzhak and Tzur Natan. Two settlers were arrested in Huwara for attacking Palestinians. Settlers also reportedly blocked Palestinian cars and hurled stones at the Efrat Junction, lightly injuring an Israeli driver. Over 1,600 settler attacks were reported in the West Bank during May.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In the Gaza Strip, Israeli military operations continue with the stated objective of "eroding Hamas's power" and disarming the organization. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir asserted that the IDF controls 60-70% of the Strip. An Israeli drone strike on a jeep in western Gaza City resulted in 4 fatalities and 6 injuries. The IDF also announced the elimination of two Hamas commanders: Sakr Abu Karim (Nukhba Force commander, involved in Oct 7 Kissufim raid) and Muhanad Othman Yassin Farwana (Hamas cell commander) in separate strikes in southern Gaza. The humanitarian situation remains critical, with al-Aqsa hospital's ICU preparing for a power outage due to dwindling fuel supplies.

Regarding ceasefire efforts, Hamas is reportedly in consultations with Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey to ensure the implementation of a ceasefire agreement. However, al-Hadath (Saudi) reported a stalemate in Hamas-Israel negotiations due to Israeli conditions and mediators' demands for Hamas to surrender all weapons. Hamas publicly praised the Kochav Ya'ir shooting attack in central Israel as "heroic."

In the West Bank, settler violence remains a concern. Two settlers were arrested in Huwara for involvement in attacks on Palestinians. Settlers also reportedly blocked Palestinian cars and threw stones at motorists at the Efrat Junction, causing light injuries to an Israeli driver who hit one of the Israelis. A Palestinian academic was abducted by Israeli forces in al-Khalil. Palestinian officials reported over 1,600 settler attacks against Palestinian civilians in the occupied West Bank during May.

LEBANON
Hezbollah launched rockets towards northern Israel, with two intercepted over Yiftah and Ramot Naftali. An explosive-laden FPV drone launched by Hezbollah injured four IDF reservists yesterday in southern Lebanon. Another Hezbollah drone struck near Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, triggering sirens in Margaliot but causing no injuries. Hezbollah claimed missile strikes against IDF vehicles in al-Adiseh on June 1 and drone swarms against IDF positions in al-Adiseh and Yahmar al-Shaqif on June 4. A Hezbollah official warned that Israel had "crossed all red lines" and threatened a powerful response to any attack on Lebanese territory.

Israel conducted significant airstrikes across Lebanon. In Beirut's Dahiyeh district, Israeli jets targeted Hezbollah command centers and infrastructure, reportedly hitting two apartments with three missiles, resulting in at least 2 killed and 11 wounded. The Israeli military stated these strikes were in response to Hezbollah's rocket fire. Evacuation warnings were issued for the southern coastal city of Tyre ahead of further airstrikes. Israeli forces also struck targets in Tyre, Mijdoun, Jabal al-Rayan, Al-Zararia, and Maarakeh in southern Lebanon. Over the weekend, the IDF reported striking approximately 150 Hezbollah infrastructure sites.

Following the Dahiyeh attack, Lebanese citizens were reported to be evacuating the area.

SYRIA & IRAQ
No direct involvement of Syria or Iraq in the ongoing Israeli-Iranian conflict has been reported in the last 24 hours. However, President Trump suggested that the US could offer aid to Syria if it chose to engage in fighting Hezbollah. In Iraq, PKK militants were reported to have killed a former PKK member in Ba'aj, Nineveh province. The Iraqi Foreign Ministry summoned the US Consul in Baghdad to deliver an official protest note regarding the treatment of Iraqi national football team player Ayman Hussein at Chicago airport, demanding clarification within 72 hours.

GULF STATES
Qatar issued a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) rerouting flights through its airspace for June 7-14, citing ongoing regional tensions. OPEC+ nations, including Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman, announced adjustments to their oil output, reaffirming their commitment to energy market stability and a cautious approach.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the downing of two Iranian one-way attack drones in the Strait of Hormuz, which were deemed a threat to international maritime traffic. Iran has instituted a fee of approximately $1.5-2 million per vessel for transit through the Strait of Hormuz, with payments accepted in various forms including Tether (cryptocurrency), goods, or services.

Saudi Arabia, through Al-Hadath TV, reported that Hezbollah members were "shocked" by the Israeli airstrikes in Dahiyeh, Beirut, as they had reportedly received assurances from Iran that the area would not be targeted. Saudi Arabia also agreed with Pakistan to boost bilateral trade volume to $10 billion. The US Department of Treasury is reportedly considering using blocked Iranian assets to help Gulf states recover from damage caused by past Iranian attacks.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Israeli Airstrikes in Beirut's Dahiyeh:** Israel attacked Hezbollah command centers and infrastructure in Beirut's Dahiyeh district, reportedly killing at least 2 and wounding 11, in response to Hezbollah rocket fire.
2.  **Iranian/Hezbollah Threats:** Iranian officials and Hezbollah vowed a "decisive and painful" response to the Dahiyeh strikes, with some threatening "True Promise 5" operations and potential targeting of Haifa and Tel Aviv.
3.  **Fatal Terrorist Attack in Central Israel:** Haim Kalomiti, 55, a reservist, was killed in a shooting spree in Kochav Ya'ir area; the attacker, Omer Yassin (21) from Tayibe, was killed by security forces.
4.  **US-Iran Confrontation in Strait of Hormuz:** US Central Command shot down two Iranian one-way attack drones threatening maritime traffic. Iran began charging ships $1.5-2 million for transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
5.  **IDF Operations Continue in Gaza & Lebanon:** IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir affirmed the goal to disarm Hamas in Gaza. The IDF also reported striking ~150 Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon over the weekend and eliminating two Hamas commanders in Gaza.
6.  **IDF Casualties in Southern Lebanon:** Cpt. Shahar Gamla (23) died from Hezbollah drone injuries, and Sgt. Ohad Yaari (21) was killed by accidental firearm discharge in separate incidents.
7.  **US Diplomacy with Iran:** President Trump stated he would not unfreeze Iranian assets or lift sanctions before a comprehensive agreement but is open to direct talks with Mojtaba Khamenei. A US-drafted resolution for the IAEA demands accurate nuclear information from Iran.
8.  **Increased Israeli Espionage on US:** The Pentagon raised its counterintelligence threat level regarding Israel to "critical" due to reports of Israeli spy agencies attempting to eavesdrop on senior US officials involved in Iran peace talks.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are significantly high following Israel's strikes in Beirut's Dahiyeh district and the subsequent strong threats of retaliation from Iran and Hezbollah, including the potential for "True Promise 5" operations targeting Haifa and Tel Aviv. This suggests an imminent threat of broader and more intense conflict. Active flashpoints include the Israel-Lebanon border, where cross-border fire and drone attacks persist, the Gaza Strip with ongoing IDF operations and a dire humanitarian situation, and the Strait of Hormuz, marked by US-Iran naval confrontations and Iran's new transit fees. The West Bank also remains an active flashpoint due to persistent settler violence and Palestinian resistance.

Military postures are shifting; Iran and Hezbollah are on high alert with explicit threats of retaliation, while Israel is also on high alert, with Prime Minister Netanyahu vowing to act decisively against any Hezbollah aggression, and the IDF Chief of Staff approving plans to deepen strikes against Hezbollah. The US maintains a military presence, with CENTCOM prepared against Iranian aggressive actions. Red lines appear to have been crossed, with Iran viewing the Dahiyeh attack as a ceasefire violation and Hezbollah asserting that Israel has crossed "all red lines." Trump's stated red lines for military action include a failure to reach an agreement swiftly or further Iranian aggression against Americans.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture remains firm, with President Trump supporting "more surgical" strikes against Hezbollah and stating he would not unfreeze Iranian assets or lift sanctions prior to a comprehensive agreement, although he expressed openness to direct talks with Mojtaba Khamenei. CENTCOM confirmed shooting down Iranian drones in the Strait of Hormuz. The US is also lobbying the IAEA for a resolution demanding accurate nuclear information from Iran and is reportedly considering using blocked Iranian assets to compensate **Gulf States** for damages. Qatar issued a NOTAM due to regional tensions, and OPEC+ agreed to cautious oil output adjustments. Al-Hadath (Saudi) reported Hezbollah was "shocked" by the Dahiyeh attack despite Iranian assurances.

Among **EU members** (and non-EU partners), France, the UK, and Norway are reportedly pursuing national sanctions against Israelis involved in West Bank violence due to a lack of consensus within the broader EU. **Russia's** Ministry of Defense claimed to have intercepted 500 Ukrainian drones, and a Russian drone reportedly struck a spent nuclear fuel storage facility near Ukraine's Chernobyl power plant. **Pakistan's** Interior Minister delivered a "special message" from PM Sharif to Mojtaba Khamenei, meeting with Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi. **Iraq's** Foreign Ministry summoned the US Consul over the treatment of an Iraqi football player.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist within the intelligence feed. Initial IDF reports of two attackers in the Kochav Ya'ir shooting were later contradicted by police and subsequent Israeli security updates confirming only one attacker. The motive and impact of the Dahiyeh attack are also disputed: Israeli sources claim to have struck Hezbollah command centers, while Al-Hadath (Saudi) suggested Hezbollah was "shocked" by the attack after Iranian assurances, and an Iranian journalist posited an "empty headquarters" was struck for symbolic reasons. The health status of Mojtaba Khamenei remains unclear, with conflicting reports from Trump (severely hurt) and an Iranian source (healthy after an old injury).

Unverified claims include NAYA (for Iraq)'s report of "coordinated missile attacks" on Israel in the coming hours, and omiddana's claims of a "night clash between America and the IRGC in Qeshm" and "Iran can't sell oil," which lack corroboration from other sources in this feed.

Propaganda indicators are evident: Iranian threats of "True Promise 5" and targeting Israeli cities serve as deterrents and morale boosters. Press TV's analytical pieces clearly align with Iranian state narratives, promoting a strong image of Iranian control and condemning US-Israeli actions. Conversely, omiddana exhibits a strong pro-Israel and anti-Iranian regime bias, celebrating Israeli strikes and mocking Iranian officials. Israeli statements emphasizing Hamas's disarmament and control over Gaza may be aimed at justifying continued operations and reassuring domestic audiences.

Reporting gaps exist regarding the precise extent of damage and casualties from the Dahiyeh strikes beyond initial figures. Official US confirmation or denial of informing Israel about the Dahiyeh strikes is not present in this feed. The full context of reported missile launches from Darab, Iran, and the specifics of the "ceasefire agreement" allegedly violated by Hamas are also not detailed. The exact reasons for the Mossad deputy head's dismissal are not fully explained beyond a routine leadership reshuffle.
